claim: There are 58 receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) in the human genome.
source: Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) are the second largest class of cell surface receptors, with 58 members in the human genome (Robinson et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Robinson et al., 2000.

claim: Binding of agonists to RTKs results in autophosphorylation of their intracellular carboxy-terminal domains.
source: Binding of agonists, typically polypeptides such as growth factors, to their extracellular amino-terminal domains results in autophosphorylation of their intracellular carboxy-terminal domains (Lemmon and Schlessinger, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lemmon and Schlessinger, 2010.

claim: Autophosphorylated RTKs signal to activate phospholipase Cγ, mitogen-activated protein kinase, and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K).
source: The autophosphorylated receptors then signal to activate phospholipase Cγ, mitogen-activated protein kinase, and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about RTK signaling pathways.

claim: Class IA PI3K coupled to RTKs are obligate heterodimers composed of regulatory p85 and catalytic p110 subunits.
source: The Class IA PI3K coupled to RTKs are obligate heterodimers composed of regulatory p85 and catalytic p110 subunits (Figure 1A; Geering et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Geering et al., 2007 and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The p85 regulatory subunit contains two SH2 domains (N-SH2 and C-SH2) separated by an inter-SH2 (iSH2) domain.
source: The p85 regulatory subunit contains two SH2 domains (N-SH2 and C-SH2) separated by an inter-SH2 (iSH2) domain.
evidence: This is stated as established structural information about the p85 subunit.

claim: The p110 catalytic subunit interacts with the entire N-SH2-iSH2-C-SH2 region of PI3K.
source: The p110 catalytic subunit interacts with the entire N-SH2-iSH2-C-SH2 region of PI3K, with the N-SH2 acting as an autoinhibitory domain to inhibit catalysis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about PI3K structure and regulation.

claim: The N-SH2 domain acts as an autoinhibitory domain to inhibit catalysis.
source: The p110 catalytic subunit interacts with the entire N-SH2-iSH2-C-SH2 region of PI3K, with the N-SH2 acting as an autoinhibitory domain to inhibit catalysis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about PI3K regulation.

claim: Binding of nerve growth factor (NGF) to TrkA triggers autophosphorylation of a pair of tyrosines.
source: For the well studying RTK tropomyosin receptor kinase A (TrkA), binding of its agonist nerve growth factor (NGF) triggers autophosphorylation of a pair of tyrosines.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TrkA signaling.

claim: Phospho-TrkA binds to the PI3K N-SH2 domain.
source: Phospho-TrkA then binds to the PI3K N-SH2.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about TrkA-PI3K interaction.

claim: Binding of phospho-TrkA to PI3K N-SH2 recruits PI3K to the plasma membrane.
source: This has the dual effect of recruiting PI3K to the PM (Thorpe et al., 2015; Ziemba et al., 2016) and causing a conformational change in p85 to relieve autoinhibition of p110 by the N-SH2 (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Thorpe et al., 2015 and Ziemba et al., 2016.

claim: Binding of phospho-TrkA to PI3K N-SH2 causes a conformational change in p85 to relieve autoinhibition of p110.
source: This has the dual effect of recruiting PI3K to the PM (Thorpe et al., 2015; Ziemba et al., 2016) and causing a conformational change in p85 to relieve autoinhibition of p110 by the N-SH2 (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2020.

claim: Activation of insulin receptor (InsR) by insulin involves autophosphorylation of tyrosines on its intracellular domain and subsequent activation of PI3K.
source: Activation of the RTK insulin receptor (InsR) by its agonist, insulin, also involves autophosphorylation of tyrosines on its intracellular domain and subsequent activation of PI3K; however, in the case of InsR, various insulin receptor substrate adaptor proteins link InsR to PI3K (Ye et al., 2017; Saltiel, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ye et al., 2017 and Saltiel, 2021.

claim: Insulin receptor substrate adaptor proteins link InsR to PI3K.
source: Activation of the RTK insulin receptor (InsR) by its agonist, insulin, also involves autophosphorylation of tyrosines on its intracellular domain and subsequent activation of PI3K; however, in the case of InsR, various insulin receptor substrate adaptor proteins link InsR to PI3K (Ye et al., 2017; Saltiel, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ye et al., 2017 and Saltiel, 2021.

claim: PI3K bound to activated RTKs on the membrane phosphorylates phosphoinositide 4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) to generate phosphoinositide 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PI(3,4,5)P3).
source: PI3K bound directly or indirectly to activated RTKs on the membrane then phosphorylates phosphoinositide 4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) to generate phosphoinositide 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PI(3,4,5)P3).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about PI3K enzymatic activity.

claim: PI(3,4,5)P3 is a signal for membrane fusion in organisms ranging from Dictyostelium to humans.
source: PI(3,4,5)P3 is a well-recognized signal for membrane fusion in organisms ranging from Dictyostelium (Nichols et al., 2015) to humans (Hawkins et al., 2006; Hawkins and Stephens, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Nichols et al., 2015, Hawkins et al., 2006, and Hawkins and Stephens, 2015.

claim: PI(3,4,5)P3-triggered membrane fusion mediates tumor cell motility.
source: Indeed, PI(3,4,5)P3-triggered membrane fusion mediates tumor cell motility, with PI3K acting as an oncoprotein and its corresponding phosphatase, PTEN, as a tumor suppressor (Hawkins et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hawkins et al., 2006.

claim: PI3K acts as an oncoprotein.
source: Indeed, PI(3,4,5)P3-triggered membrane fusion mediates tumor cell motility, with PI3K acting as an oncoprotein and its corresponding phosphatase, PTEN, as a tumor suppressor (Hawkins et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hawkins et al., 2006.

claim: PTEN acts as a tumor suppressor.
source: Indeed, PI(3,4,5)P3-triggered membrane fusion mediates tumor cell motility, with PI3K acting as an oncoprotein and its corresponding phosphatase, PTEN, as a tumor suppressor (Hawkins et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hawkins et al., 2006.

claim: NGF is an inflammatory mediator released from leukocytes in response to tissue injury and inflammation.
source: NGF is an inflammatory mediator released from leukocytes, including mast cells, eosinophils, macrophages, and lymphocytes, in response to tissue injury and inflammation (Freund-Michel and Frossard, 2008; Reis et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Freund-Michel and Frossard, 2008 and Reis et al., 2023.

claim: NGF is critical for wound healing.
source: Paradoxically, in addition to its role in increasing sensitivity to painful stimuli, NGF is also critical for wound healing (Ebadi et al., 1997; Lambiase et al., 2000; Bonini et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ebadi et al., 1997, Lambiase et al., 2000, and Bonini et al., 2002.

claim: NGF increases sensitivity to pain via a PI3K-induced increase in the number of TRPV1 ion channels in the plasma membrane of sensory neurons.
source: One of the mechanisms by which NGF increases sensitivity to pain involves a PI3K-induced increase in the number of pain-transducing TRPV1 ion channels in the plasma membrane (PM) of sensory neurons (Bonnington and McNaughton, 2003; Stein et al., 2006; Zhu and Oxford, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bonnington and McNaughton, 2003, Stein et al., 2006, and Zhu and Oxford, 2007.

claim: The NGF-stimulated rise in PI(3,4,5)P3 is much greater in cells transiently transfected with TRPV1 than in control cells without TRPV1.
source: We found that the NGF-stimulated rise in the PI3K product PI(3,4,5)P3 is much greater in cells transiently transfected with TRPV1 than in control cells without TRPV1, i.e., TRPV1 enhances NGF-mediated PI3K activity (Stratiievska et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stratiievska et al., 2018.

claim: TRPV1 enhances NGF-mediated PI3K activity.
source: We found that the NGF-stimulated rise in the PI3K product PI(3,4,5)P3 is much greater in cells transiently transfected with TRPV1 than in control cells without TRPV1, i.e., TRPV1 enhances NGF-mediated PI3K activity (Stratiievska et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stratiievska et al., 2018.

claim: TRPV1 interacts directly with PI3K (p85α and p85β subunits) via its amino-terminal ankyrin repeat domain (ARD).
source: Interestingly, TRPV1 interacts directly with PI3K (p85α and p85β subunits; Figure 1A) via its amino-terminal ankyrin repeat domain (ARD) (Stein et al., 2006) and the ARD is sufficient to increase NGF-induced PI3K activity (Stratiievska et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Stein et al., 2006 and Stratiievska et al., 2018, and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The ARD of TRPV1 is sufficient to increase NGF-induced PI3K activity.
source: Interestingly, TRPV1 interacts directly with PI3K (p85α and p85β subunits; Figure 1A) via its amino-terminal ankyrin repeat domain (ARD) (Stein et al., 2006) and the ARD is sufficient to increase NGF-induced PI3K activity (Stratiievska et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stratiievska et al., 2018.

claim: Activation of InsR by insulin signals via PI3K to activate Akt.
source: Activation of InsR by insulin signals via PI3K to activate a powerful protein kinase, Akt, which in turn regulates multiple cellular processes involved in metabolism (Saltiel, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Saltiel, 2021.

claim: Akt regulates multiple cellular processes involved in metabolism.
source: Activation of InsR by insulin signals via PI3K to activate a powerful protein kinase, Akt, which in turn regulates multiple cellular processes involved in metabolism (Saltiel, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Saltiel, 2021.

claim: Ligand-stimulated InsR endocytosis is followed by either targeting to lysosomes for degradation or recycling endosomes for reinsertion into the PM.
source: Ligand-simulated InsR endocytosis is followed by either targeting to lysosomes for degradation or recycling endosomes for reinsertion into the PM.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about InsR trafficking.

claim: InsR return to the PM is believed to involve small Rab family GTPases.
source: This return to the PM is not fully understood, but it is believed to involve small Rab family GTPases (Iraburu et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Iraburu et al., 2021.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of PI3K inhibits InsR trafficking to the PM.
source: Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K has been shown to inhibit InsR trafficking to the PM, indicating that PI3K activity is necessary for InsR homeostasis (Sasaoka et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sasaoka et al., 1999.

claim: PI3K activity is necessary for InsR homeostasis.
source: Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K has been shown to inhibit InsR trafficking to the PM, indicating that PI3K activity is necessary for InsR homeostasis (Sasaoka et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sasaoka et al., 1999.

claim: TRPV1 is expressed heavily in intracellular membranes.
source: TRPV1 is expressed heavily in intracellular membranes, making it nearly impossible to optically isolate just those channels on the PM (Liu et al., 2003; Gallego-Sandín et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2003 and Gallego-Sandín et al., 2009.

claim: The PhyB-PIF light-inducible interaction is rapid (a few tens of seconds) and fully reversible (within ~30 s).
source: The PhyB-PIF light-inducible interaction is rapid (a few tens of seconds) and fully reversible (within ~30 s) and can be repeated multiple times.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the PhyB-PIF system and is demonstrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The PhyB-PIF interaction can be repeated multiple times.
source: The PhyB-PIF light-inducible interaction is rapid (a few tens of seconds) and fully reversible (within ~30 s) and can be repeated multiple times.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the PhyB-PIF system and is demonstrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Illumination with 650 nm light induces a conformational change in PhyB that increases its affinity for PIF-YFP.
source: Illumination with 650 nm light induces a conformational change in PhyB that increases its affinity for PIF-YFP, effectively recruiting PIF-YFP to the PM.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the PhyB-PIF system and is illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The conformational change in PhyB reverses with illumination with 750 nm light.
source: The conformational change in PhyB reverses with illumination with 750 nm light, causing PIF-YFP to dissociate and return to the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the PhyB-PIF system and is illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Upon 650 nm illumination, PIF-iSH2-YFP translocated to the PM quickly while Akt-PH-CFP moved slower.
source: Upon 650 nm illumination, PIF PIF-iSH2-YFP translocated to the PM quickly (upper trace) while GRP1-PH-CFP moved slower (lower trace).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Translocation of both PIF-iSH2-YFP and GRP1-PH-CFP is reversible.
source: Translocation of both PIF-iSH2-YFP and GRP1-PH-CFP is reversible.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: NGF-induced trafficking of TRPV1 follows the increase in PM PI(3,4,5)P3 levels.
source: As shown in Figure 2A and B, the NGF-induced trafficking of TRPV1 follows the increase in PM PI(3,4,5)P3 levels.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: PI3K activation is necessary for NGF-induced trafficking of TRPV1 to the PM.
source: Although TrkA couples with PLCγ and the MAP/ERK pathways in addition to PI3K, significant evidence indicates that PI3K activation is necessary to NGF-induced trafficking of TRPV1 to the PM (Zhang et al., 2005; Stein et al., 2006; Zhu and Oxford, 2007; Stratiievska et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2005, Stein et al., 2006, Zhu and Oxford, 2007, and Stratiievska et al., 2018.

claim: Activation of the PI3K pathway is sufficient to cause TRPV1 trafficking to the PM.
source: Because PLCγ and the MAP/ERK were not directly activated by the 650 nm light, we conclude that activation of the PI3K pathway is sufficient to cause TRPV1 trafficking to the PM.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental results shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: PIF-iSH2-YFP no longer translocated to the cytoplasm in response to 750 nm light in TRPV1-expressing cells.
source: In monitoring localization of PIF-iSH2-YFP in light-activated PI3K experiments in TRPV1-expressing cells, we found that PIF-iSH2-YFP no longer translocated to the cytoplasm in response to 750 nm light (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: TRPV1 expression had no effect on a version of PIF-YFP that lacked the iSH2 domain.
source: TRPV1 expression had no effect on a version of PIF-YFP that lacked the iSH2 domain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), indicating that irreversible localization to the PM required both the iSH2 fragment of PI3K and TRPV1.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Irreversible localization of PIF to the PM required both the iSH2 fragment of PI3K and TRPV1.
source: TRPV1 expression had no effect on a version of PIF-YFP that lacked the iSH2 domain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), indicating that irreversible localization to the PM required both the iSH2 fragment of PI3K and TRPV1.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Expression of TRPM4 ion channels had no effect on 750 nm light-induced dissociation of PIF-iSH2-YFP from the PM.
source: Expression of the related TRPM4 ion channels, which do not include an ARD, also had no effect on 750 nm light-induced dissociation of PIF-iSH2-YFP from the PM (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), indicating that this effect is specific to TRPV1.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The effect of preventing PIF-iSH2-YFP dissociation from the PM is specific to TRPV1.
source: Expression of the related TRPM4 ion channels, which do not include an ARD, also had no effect on 750 nm light-induced dissociation of PIF-iSH2-YFP from the PM (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), indicating that this effect is specific to TRPV1.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The ARD of TRPV1 interacts directly with the p85 subunit of PI3K.
source: We have previously shown that the ARD of TRPV1 interacts directly with the p85 subunit of PI3K from which iSH2 is derived (Stein et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stein et al., 2006.

claim: PIF-iSH2-YFP in TRPV1-expressing cells might not dissociate from the PM when stimulated with 750 nm light because it encounters TRPV1 at the PM and binds to it.
source: We speculate that the PIF-iSH2-YFP in TRPV1-expressing cells might not dissociate from the PM when stimulated with 750 nm light because it encounters TRPV1 at the PM and binds to it, remaining bound to TRPV1 even after releasing PhyB.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation by the authors.

claim: Tet3-Bu is a tetrazine-containing amino acid which can be efficiently labeled with a cyclopropane-fused strained trans-cyclooctene (sTCO).
source: We used Tet3-Bu (Figure 3A), a tetrazine-containing amino acid which can be efficiently labeled with a cyclopropane-fused strained trans-cyclooctene (sTCO) with no detectable off-target reactivity within the time scale of our experiments (see below) (Jang et al., 2020; Jana et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jang et al., 2020 and Jana et al., 2023, and illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: Tet3-Bu has no detectable off-target reactivity within the time scale of the experiments.
source: We used Tet3-Bu (Figure 3A), a tetrazine-containing amino acid which can be efficiently labeled with a cyclopropane-fused strained trans-cyclooctene (sTCO) with no detectable off-target reactivity within the time scale of our experiments (see below) (Jang et al., 2020; Jana et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jang et al., 2020 and Jana et al., 2023.

claim: TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP and InsR-K676Tet3-Bu-GFP expressed at high levels only in transfected cells.
source: As indicated by the GFP signal and in-gel fluorescence both TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP and InsR-K676Tet3-Bu-GFP expressed at high levels only in transfected cells (Figure 3C and E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C, 3E, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP gave robust capsaicin-activated currents.
source: To test whether incorporation of Tet3-Bu interfered with the function of TRPV1, we measured capsaicin-activated currents with whole-cell voltage clamp and found that TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP gave robust capsaicin-activated currents (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: InsR-K676Tet3-Bu retained its function as measured by insulin-induced endocytosis.
source: To determine whether InsR-K676TAG protein retained its function, we measured insulin-induced endocytosis (Carpentier et al., 1992) and found endocytosis in response to insulin was maintained (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) with approximately the expected kinetics (Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and citations to Carpentier et al., 1992.

claim: sTCO-TAMRA readily equilibrated across the cell PM at the concentrations required for labeling.
source: Unfortunately, these compounds readily equilibrated across the cell PM at the concentrations required for labeling, giving indistinguishable cytosolic fluorescence in untransfected and transfected cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: sTCO-JF646 readily equilibrated across the cell PM at the concentrations required for labeling.
source: Unfortunately, these compounds readily equilibrated across the cell PM at the concentrations required for labeling, giving indistinguishable cytosolic fluorescence in untransfected and transfected cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: sTCO-fluorescein readily equilibrated across the cell PM at the concentrations required for labeling.
source: Unfortunately, these compounds readily equilibrated across the cell PM at the concentrations required for labeling, giving indistinguishable cytosolic fluorescence in untransfected and transfected cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 contains two negative charges at physiological pH to minimize passive diffusion through membrane.
source: We therefore synthesized a new sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 conjugate, which contains two negative charges at physiological pH to minimize passive diffusion through membrane and therefore selectively label membrane proteins at the cell surface (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D; Hoffmann et al., 2015; Nikić et al., 2015; Kozma et al., 2016; Lam et al., 2018; Keller et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hoffmann et al., 2015, Nikić et al., 2015, Kozma et al., 2016, Lam et al., 2018, and Keller et al., 2020, and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D.

claim: sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 did not appear to equilibrate across the cell membrane.
source: Importantly, sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 did not appear to equilibrate across the cell membrane and did not label untransfected cells (i.e. those without GFP; Figure 3—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D.

claim: sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 did not label untransfected cells.
source: Importantly, sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 did not appear to equilibrate across the cell membrane and did not label untransfected cells (i.e. those without GFP; Figure 3—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D.

claim: The reaction rate between Tet3-Bu and sTCO occurs with a rate of 2×10^4 M^−1s^−1 in vitro.
source: In vitro, the click chemistry reaction between free Tet3-Bu ncAA and sTCO occurs with a rate of 2×104 M−1s−1; this reaction rate increased by fourfold when Tet3-Bu was incorporated on the surface of GFP (Jang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jang et al., 2020.

claim: The reaction rate between Tet3-Bu and sTCO increased by fourfold when Tet3-Bu was incorporated on the surface of GFP.
source: In vitro, the click chemistry reaction between free Tet3-Bu ncAA and sTCO occurs with a rate of 2×104 M−1s−1; this reaction rate increased by fourfold when Tet3-Bu was incorporated on the surface of GFP (Jang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jang et al., 2020.

claim: The reaction rate measured for TRPV1-468Tet3-Bu-GFP and InsR-646Tet3-Bu-GFP with sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 was approximately 5×10^3 M^–1s^–1.
source: As shown in Figure 3D–F, the reaction rate we measured was approximately 5×103 M–1s–1 for both proteins, somewhat slower than expected for a protein in solution and on par with the reaction between the free amino acid and sTCO in solution (Meijer et al., 1998; Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3D-F and citations to Meijer et al., 1998 and Taylor et al., 2011.

claim: NGF induced an ~1.4-fold increase in PM Cy5 staining of TRPV1-468Tet3-Bu-GFP.
source: We observed an ~1.4-fold increase in PM Cy5 staining, indicating that NGF induced trafficking of TRPV1 to the surface (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4B-D.

claim: The total number of TRPV1 channels did not change in response to NGF, as evidenced by the total intensity of GFP fluorescence.
source: In contrast, the total number of TRPV1 channels did not change, as evidenced by the total intensity of GFP fluorescence, which was not affected by NGF.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The NGF-induced increase in surface expression measured by click chemistry (~1.4-fold) is greater than that observed in TIRF experiments (~1.1-fold).
source: This NGF-induced increase in surface expression is indeed greater than the ~1.1-fold increase in NGF-induced surface expression of TRPV1 observed in TIRF experiments (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of data from Figure 4 and Figure 2A and B.

claim: In control experiments without NGF, neither the GFP signal nor the sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 signal changed.
source: In control experiments in which cells were exposed to the vehicle (without NGF), neither the GFP signal nor the sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 signal changed (Figure 4E), indicating that the NGF-induced increase in sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 was specific to activation of the TrkA receptor by NGF.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The NGF-induced increase in sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 was specific to activation of the TrkA receptor by NGF.
source: In control experiments in which cells were exposed to the vehicle (without NGF), neither the GFP signal nor the sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 signal changed (Figure 4E), indicating that the NGF-induced increase in sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 was specific to activation of the TrkA receptor by NGF.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental results shown in Figure 4E.

claim: 750 nm light produced a small increase in sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 labeling of TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu.
source: For TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP, the sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 labeling increased slightly in response to the initial exposure to 750 nm light (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5B and D.

claim: 750 nm light produced no change in sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 labeling of InsR-K676Tet3-Bu-GFP.
source: This small increase in sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 labeling was specific to TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu, as 750 nm light produced no change in sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 labeling of InsR-K676Tet3-Bu-GFP (Figure 5F and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5F and H.

claim: The TRPV1-specific increase in labeling after 750 nm illumination is likely due to the small, irreversible PM localization of PIF-iSH2-YFP that occurs in TRPV1-expressing cells.
source: The TRPV1-specific increase in labeling after 750 nm illumination is likely due to the small, irreversible PM localization of PIF-iSH2-YFP that occurs in TRPV1-expressing cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Activation of PI3K with 650 nm light increased expression of TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu on the PM by ~1.4-fold.
source: As shown in Figure 5B–E for TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu and Figure 5F–I for InsR-K676Tet3-Bu-GFP, activation of PI3K with 650 nm light increased expression of protein on the PM. For TRPV1, the amplitude of the increase in surface expression, ~1.4-fold, was similar to that observed in click chemistry experiments in response to NGF (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5B-E.

claim: Activation of PI3K with 650 nm light increased expression of InsR-K676Tet3-Bu on the PM by ~1.4-fold.
source: Surprisingly, the increase in surface expression of InsR-K676-Tet3-Bu was also about 1.4-fold.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5F-I.

claim: PI3K activity has not been previously known to stimulate InsR delivery to the PM.
source: However, to our knowledge, PI3K activity has not been previously known to stimulate InsR delivery to the PM.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge claim by the authors.

claim: Binding of insulin to InsR is a well-studied signal for InsR endocytosis.
source: Like the NGF receptor TrkA, InsR is an RTK whose activation stimulates PI3K activity (Saltiel, 2021). Binding of insulin to InsR is a well-studied signal for InsR endocytosis (Carpentier et al., 1992), and PI3K activation downstream of InsR is key to delivery of GLUT4 transporters to the PM (Saltiel, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Carpentier et al., 1992.

claim: PI3K activation downstream of InsR is key to delivery of GLUT4 transporters to the PM.
source: Like the NGF receptor TrkA, InsR is an RTK whose activation stimulates PI3K activity (Saltiel, 2021). Binding of insulin to InsR is a well-studied signal for InsR endocytosis (Carpentier et al., 1992), and PI3K activation downstream of InsR is key to delivery of GLUT4 transporters to the PM (Saltiel, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Saltiel, 2021.

claim: Using a small ncAA and click chemistry is likely much less perturbing to protein structure and function than fusion with an ~20–30 kDa protein such as GFP, SNAP-tag, or HaloTag.
source: In addition to distinguishing proteins at the surface, using a small ncAA and click chemistry is likely much less perturbing to protein structure and function than fusion with an ~20–30 kDa protein such as GFP, SNAP-tag, or HaloTag.
evidence: This is stated as a reasoning claim by the authors.

claim: Restricting the ncAA and fluorescent label to an extracellular region/loop is less likely to interfere with protein-protein interactions on the intracellular side.
source: Restricting the ncAA and fluorescent label to an extracellular region/loop is also less likely to interfere with protein-protein interactions on the intracellular side, compared with a large protein fusion to an intracellular N- or C-terminal of a protein of interest.
evidence: This is stated as a reasoning claim by the authors.

claim: Two of four sites tested for Tet3-Bu incorporation in the S1-S2 loop of TRPV1 yielded functional, capsaicin-activated channels.
source: In our initial screen, we tested incorporation at four positions, R455, V457, K464, and T468 (Figure 3C), and used a C-terminal GFP fusion to facilitate screening. We found that TRPV1-K464Tet3-Bu-GFP and TRPV1-T468Tet3-Bu-GFP produced robust, capsaicin-activated currents when interrogated with whole-cell patch clamp (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), whereas TRPV1-R455Tet3-Bu-GFP and TRPV1-V457Tet3-Bu-GFP of incorporation did not (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Approximately one half to one third of selected sites show reasonable levels of ncAA incorporation.
source: Screening through desirable sites typically is the best approach, with approximately one half to one third of selected sites showing reasonable levels of ncAA incorporation.
evidence: This is stated as empirical knowledge by the authors based on their experience.

claim: Complete labeling with a low concentration of sTCO dye required more than 10 min.
source: As shown in Figure 3, complete labeling with a low concentration of sTCO dye required more than 10 min.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Monitoring membrane protein trafficking to the surface in real time will require a reaction that is at least 5- to 10-fold faster.
source: Monitoring membrane protein trafficking to the surface in real time will require a reaction that is at least 5- to 10-fold faster.
evidence: This is stated as a reasoning claim by the authors.

claim: Tet4 amino acids react with sTCO-based labels with rates as fast as 10^6 M^–1s^–1.
source: We have recently developed new ncAAs with the tetrazine ring more proximal to the amino acid beta carbon, which we term Tet4, that react with sTCO-based labels with rates as fast as 106 M–1s–1 (Jana et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jana et al., 2023.

claim: The aminoacyl tRNA synthetases that incorporate Tet4 amino acids into mammalian cells are not as efficient as those for Tet3 amino acids.
source: The aminoacyl tRNA synthetases that incorporate Tet4 amino acids into mammalian cells are not as efficient as those for Tet3 amino acids.
evidence: This is stated as empirical knowledge by the authors.

claim: The PhyB/PIF machinery requires supplementing cell medium with the phycocyanobilin (PCB) chromophore.
source: The PhyB/PIF machinery requires supplementing cell medium with the phycocyanobilin (PCB) chromophore, making it incompatible with in vivo experiments.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the PhyB/PIF system.

claim: Introducing four genes (PcyA, H01, Fd, and Fnr) and knocking down/out biliverdin reductase A leads to efficient synthesis of PCB in mammalian cells.
source: Introducing four genes, PcyA, H01, Fd, and Fnr, and knocking down/out biliverdin reductase A leads to efficient synthesis of PCB in mammalian cells (Uda et al., 2017; Uda et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Uda et al., 2017 and Uda et al., 2020.

claim: There is as yet no method for synthesizing the necessary ncAAs within cells.
source: However, there is as yet no method for synthesizing the necessary ncAAs within cells, precluding in vivo use of the PhyB/PIF with tetrazine-based genetic code expansion.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the current technology.

claim: PI3K is a universal signal for trafficking to the PM.
source: PI3K is a universal signal for trafficking to the PM.
evidence: This is stated as a general conclusion by the authors.

claim: In Dictyostelium, PI3K activation at the leading edge of cells underlies chemotaxis toward nutrients.
source: In Dictyostelium, PI3K activation at the leading edge of cells underlies chemotaxis toward nutrients (Nichols et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nichols et al., 2015.

claim: In macrophages, PI3K at the leading edge of cells drives motility toward the object of phagocytosis.
source: In macrophages, PI3K at the leading edge of cells drives motility toward the object of phagocytosis (Hawkins et al., 2006; Hawkins and Stephens, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hawkins et al., 2006 and Hawkins and Stephens, 2015.

claim: A vast literature has examined the mechanisms by which InsR is recycled from the PM in response to insulin.
source: A vast literature has examined the mechanisms by which InsR is recycled from the PM in response to insulin (Knutson, 1991; Ye et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2019), but less is known about ways in which delivery of InsR to the PM is regulated.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Knutson, 1991, Ye et al., 2017, and Chen et al., 2019.

claim: Less is known about ways in which delivery of InsR to the PM is regulated.
source: A vast literature has examined the mechanisms by which InsR is recycled from the PM in response to insulin (Knutson, 1991; Ye et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2019), but less is known about ways in which delivery of InsR to the PM is regulated.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap by the authors.

claim: This study demonstrates that activation of PI3K is sufficient for the first time to increase InsR in the PM.
source: We show here, for the first time, that activation of PI3K is sufficient to increase InsR in the PM.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding by the authors based on their experimental results.

claim: PI3K was identified as an important signal that enhances surface expression of TRPV1 in response to NGF.
source: For TRPV1, PI3K was identified as an important signal that enhances surface expression in response to NGF, but the steps between PI3K activation and fusion of vesicles containing TRPV1 cargo with the PM are a mystery.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: The steps between PI3K activation and fusion of vesicles containing TRPV1 cargo with the PM are a mystery.
source: For TRPV1, PI3K was identified as an important signal that enhances surface expression in response to NGF, but the steps between PI3K activation and fusion of vesicles containing TRPV1 cargo with the PM are a mystery.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap by the authors.

claim: The iSH2 domain has been previously expressed as a fusion protein with PIF and has been shown to reversibly translocate to the PM and activate PI3K in response to light.
source: The iSH2 domain has been previously expressed as a fusion protein with PIF and has been shown to reversibly translocate to the PM and activate PI3K in response to light (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Levskaya et al., 2009; Toettcher et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Levskaya et al., 2009 and Toettcher et al., 2011, and illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The iSH2 domain associates with the endogenous p110 catalytic subunit of PI3K.
source: It has previously been shown that the iSH2 domain associates with the endogenous p110 catalytic subunit of PI3K (Klippel et al., 1993).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Klippel et al., 1993.

claim: The iSH2-p110 heterodimer is missing the autoinhibitory domains of p85 and is constitutively active.
source: Because this heterodimer is missing the autoinhibitory domains of p85, it is constitutively active, so that PI3K phosphorylates its substrate, PI(4,5)P2 to make PI(3,4,5)P3 whenever the PIF-iSH2-YFP is driven to the membrane (Figure 1C; Suh et al., 2006; Idevall-Hagren et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Suh et al., 2006 and Idevall-Hagren et al., 2012, and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: TRPV1-expressing cells were incubated in serum-deprived medium for 24 hr before insulin receptor endocytosis experiments.
source: F-11 cells expressing InsR-K676TAG-GFP were treated with 30 µM Tet3.0-Bu in the culture medium for 24 hr, transferred to glass coverslip, and further cultured in serum-deprived medium for 24 hr.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: Labeling of the insulin receptor and insulin treatment were performed at around 35°C to promote the rate of endocytosis.
source: Labeling of the receptor and insulin treatment were performed at around 35°C to promote the rate of endocytosis using a local perfusion system with heat exchanger (Koh et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with a citation to Koh et al., 2011.
